newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SURVEY SEES S.AFRICA Q2 BUSINESS CONFIDENCE FALL.
newsitem.headline: SURVEY SEES S.AFRICA Q2 BUSINESS CONFIDENCE FALL.

text.p: The latest survey by the Bureau for Economic Research at the University of Stellenbosch shows a sharp decline in South African business confidence in the second quarter of this year.

The BER said in a statement on Thursday that this negated improvements in the previous two quarters with its business confidence index value dropping from 45.2 percent during the first quarter to 34.4 percent in the second quarter, which was the same level it had been at in the third quarter of 1996.
"The sharpest declines in business confidence were reported in the wholesale, motor trade, manufacturing, building and construction sectors," the BER said.
The wholesale sector reported sharply lower orders although the growth in sales was slightly better than expected.
In the motor trade, sales of new and used vehicles were below expectations, stocks piled up and new vehicle orders were sharply lower, it said.
The manufacturing sector reported that sales and orders were below expectations, as were exports. Stocks of finished goods increased while production volumes declined.
"Export selling prices increased at a rate slower than was expected, probably due to the stronger rand exchange rate," the BER said.
"As a result, profit margins came under pressure. Short term expectations relating to both domestic sales and exports were adjusted downwards."
Work on hand in the building and construction sector declined. In the non-residential sector, tendering competition increased while the residential sector remained sluggish.
But the survey did pinpoint some positive aspects, BER said.
"General business conditions in the retail sector stabilised and the improvement in business confidence reported during the first quarter was maintained," it said.
Sales volumes were better than expected but the wholesale sector reported sluggish growth in orders and it seemed as if higher sales came out of existing stocks.
Manufacturing volumes still showed significant positive growth on a year-on-year basis and this was expected to continue in the third quarter, it said.
"Admittedly, expectations were adjusted to more realistic levels, given the situation in the wholesale and retail sectors," the BER said.
"Fixed investment plans and export expectations remain positive and an encouraging factor regarding general economic prospects for the year."
